test_title: RRB NTPC CBT-I Official Paper (Held On: 1 Mar 2021 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: Which of the following is related to the 61st Amendment of the Constitution of India?

options.text: Advancement of economically weaker sections of citizens
Extended the period of reservation of seats
Incorporation of Goa, Daman and Diu as a union territory
Lowered the voting age of elections

solution:
The correct answer is __**Lowered the voting age of elections**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The **61st Amendment of the Constitution of India**, passed in **1988**, **lowered the voting age from 21 years to 18 years**.
 
• The amendment was made to **increase youth participation in the democratic process** and ensure their representation in elections.
 
• It amended Article 326 of the Constitution, which originally set the minimum age for voting at **21 years**.
 
• This change in the voting age was implemented for **all national and state elections in India**.
 
• The change also sought to align India's voting age with that of many other democratic nations.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Article 326** of the Indian Constitution:

 
 
• It lays down the qualifications for the right to vote in India.
 
• Before the 61st Amendment, Article 326 required a minimum age of 21 for voting in elections.
 
 
 
• The **61st Amendment Act of 1988** marked a significant change in the democratic process by **empowering a larger section of the population** to actively participate in electing representatives.
 
• The **Electoral Roll** is updated by the Election Commission of India, ensuring that all eligible voters, including those who turned 18 after the amendment, are registered.
 
• The **Indian Youth** now represent a significant portion of the electorate, which has brought about changes in the political landscape.
 
• The 61st Amendment is part of a series of **constitutional reforms** aimed at making India’s democratic system more inclusive and representative.
